title: Pairs Whose Sum Is Divisible by d

concept.title: The partner of a remainder
body: Two numbers `x` and `y` have a sum divisible by `d` exactly when their remainders add up to `0` or to `d`: the remainder of `y` must be `(d - x % d) % d`, the **complement** of the remainder of `x`. Count how many earlier numbers have each remainder, and when you read `x`, add the count of the complement.

The outer `% d` makes the complement of remainder 0 again 0 (two multiples of `d` add up to a multiple of `d`) and keeps `d - r` below `d`. When `r` is exactly half of `d`, the number pairs with other numbers of the same remainder, which the same formula covers.

statement: Given `n` positive integers and a number `d`, count the pairs of positions `i < j` for which `a[i] + a[j]` is divisible by `d`.
hints: Look at the remainders when dividing by d.
The partner of remainder r has remainder `(d - r) % d`.
Count the earlier numbers with each remainder in a map.

# Your code here

explanation: Two numbers have a sum divisible by `d` exactly when their remainders are complements of each other. A map of remainder counts gives the earlier partners.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, d = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

count = {}
total = 0
for x in a:
    rem = x % d
    total += count.get((d - rem) % d, 0)
    count[rem] = count.get(rem, 0) + 1
print(total)
